name: BLS International Services Ltd
title: BLS International Services Ltd - 540073 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consolidated revenue up 32% to INR 973 crore but EBITDA margin fell to 25.5% from 28.9% on Digital mix (7.4% margin); Visa segment EBITDA up 11% at 41.9% margin, with no capacity or capex disclosure.

triggers.quote: Digital Services contributed about 48%. A year ago, the mix was 62% and 38%, respectively.

summary.headline: BLS Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record INR 973 crores (+32% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 25.5% from 28.9% on Digital mix shift.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 973 crores and EBITDA rose 17% to INR 248 crores. Margin compression came from Digital Services, now 48% of revenue after the Atyati consolidation, carrying a lower margin than Visa & Consular. Visa & Consular grew 11% in revenue and EBITDA with a 41.9% margin, while net revenue per application rose 10% to INR 3,553. Management reiterated an FY30 ambition of INR 6,300-6,500 crores revenue and 28-30% EBITDA margin, and fielded repeated questions on buybacks and valuation, which were deferred to the Board.

segments.name: Visa & Consular Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 510 crores (+11%), EBITDA INR 214 crores (+11%), margin 41.9%. H1 revenue INR 1,070 crores (+16%), EBITDA INR 440 crores, margin 41.1%. About 11 lakh applications in Q2; net revenue per application INR 3,553 (+10%).

segments.name: Digital Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 463 crores (+66%), EBITDA INR 34 crores (+67%), margin 7.4%. Growth from business correspondent and loan distribution plus full-quarter Atyati. H1 revenue INR 793 crores (+50%), EBITDA INR 61 crores, margin 7.7%. BC GTV about INR 41,400 crores in Q2 and over INR 70,900 crores in H1; loan disbursements over INR 9,500 crores in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Net revenue per application expected to grow about 5-6% annually, driven by better pricing on new contracts and new services.
Visa & Consular targeted at 60-65% of business over time, with Digital Services the balance.
Visa & Consular EBITDA margin seen stabilising around 38-40%; scope to improve Digital margins over time.
Target growth of at least 15% for Visa & Consular, driven by travel demand, value-added services and new contracts.
FY30 ambition: revenue INR 6,300-6,500 crores, 20-25% annual growth, EBITDA margin 28-30%, via Visa growth, new contracts, iDATA and CI, Digital and G2C scaling, and selective acquisitions.
No further hotel investment until existing hotels are assessed over the next one to two years. Buyback proposal under Board consideration, no decision yet.
risks_watch: Visa application volumes down about 3% YoY on Middle East geopolitics; watch whether Q3 seasonal recovery occurs as management expects.
Digital Services margin at 7.4% is diluting consolidated margin (25.5% vs 28.9%); watch the Digital margin trajectory.
Hotel business in London performing weakly per an analyst; management will reassess over the next one to two years.
Buyback decision pending with Board; repeated analyst pressure on capital deployment with INR 1,556 crores net cash.
Media articles on Spain, Slovakia and Vietnam were raised; management denies issues but cannot control future coverage.
E-visa adoption by governments is a potential risk to revenue per application, per an analyst question.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FY30 ambition, but guarded and deferential on buybacks, valuation and the hotel business, which were repeatedly deflected to the Board or to later review. Responses on press articles and e-visa were brief and reassuring rather than quantified.
key_quotes: In Q2, revenue reached a record INR 973 crores, an increase of 32% over last year.
We believe the EBITDA margin in the Visa business has stabilised at around 38% to 40%.
Our target is to sustain growth of at least 15%.
As we have explained earlier, we are deploying our cash towards expanding our existing businesses and pursuing selected M&A opportunities that are currently in our pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is the company expecting in net revenue per application now that most of the transition is complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net revenue per application to grow about 5-6% annually, driven by better pricing on new contracts and new services.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected split of growth between Visa and Digital, and will Visa margins expand to lift consolidated margin back to 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Over time Visa & Consular is expected to be about 60-65% of business with Digital the balance. Management said Visa EBITDA margin has stabilised at around 38-40%, with scope to improve Digital margins; consolidated Q2 margin was about 25.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did application volumes fall about 3% YoY and Visa revenue fall about 9% QoQ? Is that seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: The YoY decline was mainly due to Middle East geopolitics. Management confirmed Q1 is typically the highest-volume quarter, with seasonal moderation in Q2 and Q3 every year, in addition to the geopolitical effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further developments on Spain, Slovakia, Vietnam and other media reports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no issue with Spain, Slovakia or Vietnam and that it had clarified this in the investor presentation; it cannot control future press articles.

qa_highlights.question: Will e-visa adoption by governments reduce revenue per application and profitability, and are new outsourcing bids pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said countries it serves do not offer e-visa models and it continues to assist governments on different models. On bids, it said it is participating across Europe and other regions, with the government count at 46 expected to rise and wins to be announced once finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the next leg of Visa & Consular growth, and what has converted from the USD 1-2 billion tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 15% Visa & Consular growth from travel demand, value-added services and new contracts. Recent first-time wins cited include Slovakia, Italy, Portugal, Poland, Germany and a INR 2,500 crores UIDAI Aadhaar contract; no pipeline conversion figure was given.

capex_capacity: Hotel business: no further hotel investment until existing hotels are assessed over the next one to two years; London hotel acquired last year was cited by an analyst as weak.

Capacity framing: BLS operates across more than 100 countries, processed around 500 million applications globally during Q2, and works with 46 governments (confirmed by management); Aadhaar Seva Kendra operated under UIDAI contract.
Digital network: more than 1,88,200 touch points at end-September; supports more than 1,000 government citizen services through technology and last-mile network.

Capital deployment: net cash INR 1,556 crores at 30 September 2026; capital priority to strengthening existing businesses or complementary capabilities; buyback proposal under Board consideration, no decision announced.

Tender pipeline: management said it is actively participating in tenders across Europe, North America and other markets; new contract wins (Portugal, Poland, Slovakia, Italy, Germany, and INR 2,500 crores UIDAI Aadhaar contract) cited, with no fresh quantified timeline.
demand_pricing: Visa & Consular application volumes down about 3% YoY in Q2, which management attributed to Middle East geopolitics, plus a typical Q2/Q3 seasonal moderation; Q2 applications about 11 lakh.
Net revenue per application rose 10% YoY to INR 3,553 in Q2, driven by better pricing on new contracts and higher value-added services; H1 net revenue per application INR 3,537 (+11%).
Visa & Consular Q2 revenue INR 510 crores (+11%) with 52% share of consolidated revenue, down from 62% a year ago; Digital Services Q2 revenue INR 463 crores (+66%), 48% share versus 38%.

Digital Services BC GTV about INR 41,400 crores in Q2 and over INR 70,900 crores in H1; loan disbursements over INR 9,500 crores in Q2; growth from business correspondent and loan distribution plus full-quarter Atyati consolidation.
Management guided Visa & Consular growth of at least 15%, and net revenue per application growth of about 5-6% annually; FY30 ambition of 20-25% annual revenue growth to INR 6,300-6,500 crores.

growth.why: Management guides Visa & Consular growth of at least 15% and an FY30 ambition of INR 6,300-6,500 crores (20-25% annual growth), backed partly by pricing on new contracts (net revenue per application +10%), new contracts and tender pipeline, but no quantified capacity additions and hotel investment is paused.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 25.5% in Q2 from 28.9% as Digital (48% of revenue, 7.4% margin) diluted mix; Visa margin is stabilising at 38-40% and Digital margin improvement is only 'over time', so expansion back toward 28-30% depends on Digital margins rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches were quantified; hotel investment is paused for one to two years, and the 1,88,200 touch points and 46 governments are existing capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Visa application volumes fell about 3% YoY in Q2 (about 11 lakh applications) on Middle East geopolitics and seasonality, so volume growth is not assured; Visa growth of at least 15% is guided mainly through pricing and new contracts.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital priority is strengthening existing businesses, no further hotel investment until assessment over one to two years, and capex was not discussed; net cash is INR 1,556 crores, but the capex-led growth path is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 29% and Q2 grew 32%, with management guiding Visa growth of at least 15%, and the FY30 ambition of INR 6,300-6,500 crores implies 20-25% annual growth, but no near-term guidance raise was stated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Visa volumes were down 3% YoY and Q3 seasonal recovery is unproven amid Middle East geopolitics; Digital margin dilution (7.4%) is already pulling consolidated margin to 25.5%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited value-added services and new services supporting net revenue per application growth of 5-6% annually, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: New government and Visa contract wins converting to revenue
rows.why: Recent first-time wins cited include Slovakia, Italy, Portugal, Poland, Germany and a INR 2,500 crores UIDAI Aadhaar contract, with the government count at 46 expected to rise, though no pipeline conversion figure or fresh timeline was given.

rows.label: Net revenue per application growth of 5-6% annually
rows.why: Net revenue per application rose 10% YoY to INR 3,553 in Q2 on better pricing for new contracts, and management guides 5-6% annual growth from the same drivers.

rows.label: Digital margin improvement
rows.why: Digital EBITDA margin is 7.4% in Q2 (INR 34 crores on INR 463 crores), and management says there is scope to improve it, with no timeline or target given.

tone.note: Management was confident on Visa growth of at least 15% and the FY30 ambition, but deflected buybacks, valuation and the London hotel to the Board, while analysts pressed on capital deployment, Digital margin dilution and press reports on Spain, Slovakia and Vietnam.
